html:
The Uwottüja, known in Spanish as the Piaroa, are an Indigenous people of the middle Orinoco in southern Venezuela, with some communities across the river in Colombia. They live along the Sipapo, Cataniapo and other tributaries in Amazonas state.

They farm manioc and other crops in forest gardens, hunt and fish. Anthropologists know them for a strongly peaceful way of life that prizes self-control and cooperation, and for their shamans' long chants and knowledge of plants. Like other peoples of the region, such as the Ye'kwana and Yanomami, they have faced missions, rubber collectors and, in recent decades, illegal gold mining. They are among the larger Indigenous peoples of Venezuela.
